text:
maria: Heads-up — noticed p95/p99 tail spikes for streamed responses when the batcher coalesces partial-decode flows and we do a kernel switch mid-send. Looks like stitch + kernel-selector + kv-prefetch interplay. Putting initial traces here.
ashwin: Can you paste a trace id and a couple of numbers (p50/p95/p99) from the run that shows the regression?
maria: trace=stitch/2026-03-18/aa3f4f. Baseline p95=92ms, regressed run p95=280ms, p99=640ms. Quick flame: partial-decode scheduling + kernel handoff hotspots.
jon: Do we have KV hit-rate around those spikes? My gut says KV prefetch eviction -> blocking prefetch -> stalls while kernel swaps.
maria: KV sample around the spikes: hit-rate dropped from 96%->72% for affected prefixes. Microprofile snippet:
```
[stitch] enqueue partial-decode: 2026-03-18T12:10:01.123
[kv] prefetch miss -> blocking fetch +14ms
[kernel] handoff start +120ms
[stitch] flush start +40ms
```
ashwin: Two quick levers to try: 1) limit coalescing token budget so fewer long-lived merged batches; 2) pin kernel for the lifetime of the stream until KV warm-up threshold. Config names: `batch.coalesce_token_budget`, `kernel.pin_until_kv_warm`.
maria: Tried `batch.coalesce_token_budget=16` locally — p95 improved to ~140ms but overall throughput dropped ~6% because we sent more small kernels. Cost up though latency better.
jon: Another axis: flush cadence + partial-decode scheduling. Right now we do eager early-flush when partial-decode ready; that interacts poorly with kernel switch. Could try `soft_flush` where we jitter 10-30ms and let small batches accumulate unless kernel-change pending.
maria: Thinking aloud: stitch window = min(linger_ms, token_budget / average_tokens_per_req). But fairness: starving tiny streams if token_budget too small.
perf-bot: :rotating_light: perf-regression alert (commit abc123): streaming p95 +36% vs baseline on nightly perf-suite.
ashwin: If we combine kernel pinning until KV-hit% >= 90% and soft_flush jitter, we might avoid the double penalty (eviction + handoff). Kernel pinning heuristic: pin until `kv.hit_rate(window=5s) >= 0.9` or `pin_max_ms=200`.
jon: I'll spin a canary with pinning+jitter on dedicated pool `stitch-canary-3`. Will capture per-request KV hit-rate, partial-decode queue length and kernel-switch counts. Expect ~30m run.
maria: Please also log batch sizes distribution and `coalesce_token_budget` in the canary. If we can get a clear delta on p99 tail we'll be in good shape. :thumbsup:
jon: started canary run at 2026-03-18T12:11:00Z on stitch-canary-3. Posting results when done.
ashwin: If canary looks good, follow-up: add a short-lived experiment to reduce `coalesce_token_budget` for streaming routes only, and enable `kernel.pin_until_kv_warm` behind feature flag.
maria: Sounds good. Also let's avoid broad config flips — small scoped flags per-route. Will collect sample prompts for repro and pin in the ticket.
jon: canary finished. Quick numbers: p95 dropped from 280ms->108ms with pin+jitter, KV hit-rate recovered to 94% within 1.2s, kernel-switches per-1000 reqs down from 17->4. Raw logs uploaded to /perf/artifacts/2836547890-canary.log
maria: Nice, can you also export the trace for a slow request from the canary? I want to see if any residual stalls remain.
jon: uploaded: /perf/traces/2836547890/trace-1.json. Looks like a few 30-40ms stalls due to k-v fetch outliers — still worth investigating but huge improvement overall.
ashwin: Next steps: prod canary for a subset of streaming routes with `coalesce_token_budget=24`, `kernel.pin_until_kv_warm=true`, and `soft_flush_jitter=10-30ms`. Also add an eval to measure unit cost impact.
maria: Opening a follow-up runbook/ticket with the artifacts and recommended safe default flags. Thanks all.
